general.description: Every configured MCP server, no shell. What you get with no profiles file at all.

repository.description: Work in a checked-out project and its history. The consequential git commands stop for a person — push, reset, clean, checkout, commit, rebase, merge, rm, branch -D, stash drop. That list is an aid, not a boundary: git has other spellings for the same effects, so the sandbox is what makes a miss survivable. Plans with todos, and drops old command output once the conversation gets long.
repository.system_prompt: You are working inside a git repository. Read before you write, and say plainly when you cannot verify something rather than assuming it.

analysis.description: Read data files and summarise them. No interpreter, deliberately — computing over the data would need one. The allowlist governs which executables may run and says nothing about redirection, so a listed command can still write with `>`; the sandbox bounds where.
analysis.system_prompt: You are examining data. State the shape and provenance of what you read before drawing conclusions from it.

research.description: Search and read. Deliberately no shell — that pair is the injection path 0.2.0 removed.
research.system_prompt: You are researching. Cite what you read, and say plainly when a source does not answer the question.
